LiteRT's AOT compilation is what solves the on-device JIT first-run penalty. It is a paid commercial product with a 14-day trial; pricing is not public. Strategic read for the owner: if NPU acceleration is genuinely wanted, the industry's direction of travel is LiteRT multi-vendor, not QNN single-vendor — the Qualcomm-only path is the one a specialist just exited. A commercial SDK also conflicts with a $4.99 one-time price unless per-unit economics work out.

open_questions: Licensing is the hardest blocker and I could not resolve it publicly: the HF model cards declare apache-2.0, but Qualcomm AI Hub NPU assets are elsewhere described as under the Qualcomm AI Model & Software License, and the QAIRT runtime .so files carry separate SDK terms. Redistributing all three inside a paid Play Store app needs explicit written confirmation from ai-hub-support@qti.qualcomm.com before any engineering spend.

Model download size is unverified — the S3 asset host was unreachable from this sandbox. An 809M-parameter model at W8 weights implies roughly 800 MB+, which would be 4x+ the current 190 MB multi download on a metered connection. Worth a manual HEAD request on the 8 Gen 3 zip before anything else, since this alone may disqualify the tier on download burden.

Whether re-exporting with a reduced AUDIO_EMB_LEN (the QNN analogue of audio_ctx=512) is viable. It requires forking ai-hub-models, changing constants that also drive the cross-attention KV cache shapes, re-running AIMET w8a16 quantization, and recompiling per chipset — with no guarantee the quantized encoder re-quantizes cleanly. This is the only path that would make a QNN tier architecturally compatible, and it is a research spike, not an integration task.

Real-world WER on noisy dictation for the w8a16 turbo model. Qualcomm's 0.15%-of-float claim is LibriSpeech (clean read speech) and generically about 'our whisper model'. The owner's users dictate in real environments — and one developer already reported outright token divergence between QNN and PyTorch on the official precompiled asset.

Whether Whisper-Small-Quantized on NPU (270 ms encoder) actually beats the current whisper.cpp small q5_1 with audio_ctx=512 on the Z Fold6 for typical 1–3 s segments. This is measurable in a day with the free AI Hub hosted-device tier and is the single highest-value experiment — but note it is a same-model runtime swap, not the premium tier above multi that was originally envisioned.

Whether Qualcomm intends to publish a first-party Android Whisper sample now that the Argmax link is dead, and whether the AI Hub 'not supported on any chipset' page state is a transient bug or reflects real deprecation of the mobile target for this model. Worth asking directly in the AI Hub Slack community before committing.
field.bottom_line: Recommend against shipping the Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo Quantized NPU tier, on the strength of one number and one structural fact. The number: Qualcomm's own model card puts the encoder at 1,421 ms on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 — the Z Fold6's exact SoC — and it never drops below ~1,130 ms on any mobile chip including the newest 8 Elite Gen 5, so this is a model-shape problem, not a device problem. The structural fact: the exported graph hardcodes a 30-second input window (CHUNK_LENGTH=30, AUDIO_EMB_LEN=1500, encoder TensorSpec fixed at 3000 mel frames), so every segment is zero-padded to 30 s and a 0.3-second 'yes' costs the same ~1.34 s as a full sentence. That directly cancels the audio_ctx=512 optimization that made the multi tier feel 'almost instantaneous' — QNN has no per-call equivalent. A tier marketed as faster-than-default would be roughly an order of magnitude slower per commit. The field evidence points the same way. Argmax built exactly this — Whisper on Qualcomm NPU for Android, in official collaboration with Qualcomm AI Hub, shipped to the Play Store — and archived the repo on 2026-01-24, citing Snapdragon-only device coverage and a first-run JIT penalty, moving to multi-vendor Google LiteRT instead. Qualcomm now has no first-party Android Whisper sample at all: the only Whisper app in ai-hub-apps is a Windows Python script, and the Android directory's Speech-to-Text entry is a dead link to that archived repo. So the 'we'd be first' marketing angle is technically available, but it is available because the best-resourced attempt was made and retired — and that is a question a reviewer will ask. Two things are worth salvaging. First, if NPU is still desired, the only defensible candidate is Whisper-Small-Quantized: same openai/whisper-small base checkpoint as the current multi tier, 268–270 ms encoder on 8 Gen 3 — 5.3x faster than the turbo. Measure it against the existing audio_ctx=512 CPU path before anything else; it is a day of work on AI Hub's free hosted devices and it either kills the idea cleanly or produces the one real datapoint that matters. Be clear-eyed that this is a runtime swap of the model already shipping, not the premium tier above multi that was originally imagined. Second, resolve licensing before any engineering spend: sample code is clean BSD-3-Clause, but the model weights (cards say apache-2.0, Qualcomm elsewhere says AI Model & Software License) and the QAIRT runtime .so files carry different and possibly conflicting terms for redistribution in a paid app. Secondary but real costs if this proceeds anyway: a per-chipset binary matrix pinned to QAIRT versions, a hard Hexagon v73 device floor, an unverified but likely 800 MB+ download versus today's 190 MB, and a maintained whisper.cpp fallback that never goes away. The current architecture already fits the hardware well; this particular model does not fit the architecture.
